subproblem.title: Implicit function theorem: local C¹ graph chart of the regular part of a level set of a C¹ function on ℝ^{n+1}
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} open, F : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ of class C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 F), and y₀ ∈ W with DF(y₀) ≠ 0. Then there exist an open set D ⊆ ℝⁿ, a map Λ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+1}, a point c ∈ ℝⁿ, a real ρ and an open set N ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} such that: Λ is C¹ on D and injective on D; for every z ∈ D, Λ(z) ∈ W, F(Λ(z)) = F(y₀), DΛ(z) (= fderiv ℝ Λ z) is injective and DΛ(z)(ℝⁿ) = ker DF(Λ(z)); the closed ball B̄_ρ(c) is contained in D; y₀ ∈ N; and every y ∈ N with F(y) = F(y₀) is of the form y = Λ(z) with z in the open ball B_ρ(c).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (W : Set (Euclid (n + 1))) (F : Euclid (n + 1) → ℝ) (y₀ : Euclid (n + 1)), IsOpen W → ContDiff ℝ 1 F → y₀ ∈ W → fderiv ℝ F y₀ ≠ 0 → ∃ (D : Set (Euclid n)) (Λ : Euclid n → Euclid (n + 1)) (c : Euclid n) (ρ : ℝ) (N : Set (Euclid (n + 1))), IsOpen D ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Λ D ∧ InjOn Λ D ∧ (∀ z ∈ D, Λ z ∈ W ∧ F (Λ z) = F y₀ ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ Λ z) ∧ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Λ z : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid (n + 1)) = LinearMap.ker (fderiv ℝ F (Λ z) : Euclid (n + 1) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)) ∧ closedBall c ρ ⊆ D ∧ IsOpen N ∧ y₀ ∈ N ∧ N ∩ F ⁻¹' {F y₀} ⊆ Λ '' ball c ρ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 2 (local graph parametrization of Γ_t by straightening F with the inverse function theorem; Simon Ch. 2, 6.3–6.4 and Remark 4.4, Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 “if”), for one point y₀, with the neighbourhood N made explicit. The parent straightens with the coordinates y_l (l ≠ i) where ∂_iF(y₀) ≠ 0; here any linear π satisfying (★) below is used — the parent's coordinate projection is one such π, and the Lean-convenient choice is described in step 2. Notation: ℓ := DF(y₀) = fderiv ℝ F y₀, t := F(y₀), K := ker ℓ ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}. Extra import needed in Lean: Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.InverseFunctionTheorem.ContDiff.

1. Dimension of K. Since ℓ ≠ 0 there is v₀ with ℓ(v₀) ≠ 0, and every r ∈ ℝ equals ℓ((r/ℓ(v₀))·v₀); so ℓ is onto ℝ. By rank–nullity (LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker), 1 + dim K = n + 1, so dim K = n = dim ℝⁿ.

2. A complementary linear map π. Let e : K → ℝⁿ be a linear isomorphism (LinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq, using step 1) and let g : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝⁿ be a linear map extending e, i.e. g(v) = e(v) for v ∈ K (LinearMap.exists_extend). Let π := g, viewed as a continuous linear map (finite dimension; LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap). Then
 (★) if ℓ(v) = 0 and π(v) = 0, then v = 0,
 because v ∈ K and e(v) = π(v) = 0 with e injective. (If ∂_iF(y₀) ≠ 0, the parent's choice π(y) = (y_l)_{l≠i} also satisfies (★): v ∈ K with v_l = 0 for l ≠ i gives 0 = ℓ(v) = v_i ∂_iF(y₀), so v = 0.)

3. Straightening map. Define Θ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝⁿ × ℝ by Θ(y) := (π(y), F(y)). Θ is C¹ (π is linear, F is C¹), and for every y it has derivative DΘ(y) = π × DF(y), the map v ↦ (π v, DF(y) v) (ContinuousLinearMap.prod; HasFDerivAt.prodMk).

4. Invertible derivative near y₀. The linear map A₀ := π × ℓ is injective by (★), and dim ℝ^{n+1} = n + 1 = dim(ℝⁿ × ℝ), so A₀ is bijective (LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective_of_finrank_eq_finrank), i.e. A₀ is (the underlying map of) a continuous linear equivalence E₀ : ℝ^{n+1} ≃ ℝⁿ × ℝ (LinearEquiv.ofBijective, LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv). Let O be the set of y such that π × DF(y) is (the underlying map of) a continuous linear equivalence ℝ^{n+1} ≃ ℝⁿ × ℝ. The map y ↦ π × DF(y) is continuous (DF is continuous because F is C¹, ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, and (L₁, L₂) ↦ L₁ × L₂ is the linear isometry ContinuousLinearMap.prodₗᵢ), and the set of invertible continuous linear maps is open (ContinuousLinearEquiv.isOpen); hence O is open, and y₀ ∈ O.

5. Inverse function theorem. Since Θ is C¹ at y₀ with derivative E₀, the C¹ inverse function theorem (ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph) gives an open partial homeomorphism Φ₀ with Φ₀ = Θ as functions (ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_coe, which holds by rfl) and y₀ ∈ source(Φ₀) (ContDiffAt.mem_toOpenPartialHomeomorph_source). Restrict it to the open set O ∩ W (OpenPartialHomeomorph.restrOpen): we get an open partial homeomorphism Φ, still equal to Θ as a function, with source(Φ) = source(Φ₀) ∩ O ∩ W (so y₀ ∈ source(Φ)), open source and open target, and inverse Φ⁻¹ = Φ.symm satisfying Φ⁻¹(a) ∈ source(Φ) and Θ(Φ⁻¹(a)) = a for a ∈ target(Φ), and Φ⁻¹(Θ(y)) = y, Θ(y) ∈ target(Φ) for y ∈ source(Φ).

6. Definition of the chart. Put D := {z ∈ ℝⁿ : (z, t) ∈ target(Φ)}, which is open (preimage of the open target under the continuous map z ↦ (z, t)); Λ(z) := Φ⁻¹(z, t) for every z ∈ ℝⁿ (Φ⁻¹ = Φ.symm is a total function; its values for z ∉ D are never used); and c := π(y₀).

7. Values of Λ. Let z ∈ D. Then Λ(z) ∈ source(Φ) ⊆ O ∩ W and Θ(Λ(z)) = (z, t), i.e. π(Λ(z)) = z and F(Λ(z)) = t = F(y₀). In particular Λ(z) ∈ W.

8. Injectivity on D. If z, z' ∈ D and Λ(z) = Λ(z'), then z = π(Λ(z)) = π(Λ(z')) = z' by step 7.

9. Differentiability. Let z ∈ D and a := (z, t) ∈ target(Φ). Since Λ(z) = Φ⁻¹(a) ∈ O, there is a continuous linear equivalence E with E = π × DF(Λ(z)) = DΘ(Φ⁻¹(a)). By OpenPartialHomeomorph.hasFDerivAt_symm, Φ⁻¹ has derivative E⁻¹ at a, and by OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm (Θ is C¹ at Φ⁻¹(a)) Φ⁻¹ is C¹ at a. The map z ↦ (z, t) is smooth with derivative inl : w ↦ (w, 0). By the chain rule Λ is C¹ at z and DΛ(z) = E⁻¹ ∘ inl. As this holds at every z ∈ D, Λ is C¹ on D.

10. Injective derivative. DΛ(z) = E⁻¹ ∘ inl is a composition of injective maps, hence injective.

11. Range of DΛ(z). If v = DΛ(z)(w) = E⁻¹(w, 0), then (π v, DF(Λ(z)) v) = E v = (w, 0), so DF(Λ(z)) v = 0. Conversely, if DF(Λ(z)) v = 0, then E v = (π v, 0), so v = E⁻¹(π v, 0) = DΛ(z)(π v). Hence DΛ(z)(ℝⁿ) = ker DF(Λ(z)). (Equivalently: F∘Λ ≡ t on the open set D gives DΛ(z)(ℝⁿ) ⊆ ker DF(Λ(z)), and both spaces are n-dimensional because DΛ(z) is injective and DF(Λ(z)) ≠ 0, E being invertible.)

12. The closed ball. c ∈ D, since (c, t) = (π(y₀), F(y₀)) = Θ(y₀) = Φ(y₀) ∈ target(Φ) because y₀ ∈ source(Φ). As D is open, choose ε > 0 with B_ε(c) ⊆ D (Metric.isOpen_iff) and put ρ := ε/2 > 0. Then B̄_ρ(c) ⊆ B_ε(c) ⊆ D.

13. The neighbourhood N. Put N := source(Φ) ∩ π⁻¹(B_ρ(c)). It is open (source(Φ) is open and π is continuous), and y₀ ∈ N because y₀ ∈ source(Φ) and π(y₀) = c with ρ > 0. Let y ∈ N with F(y) = F(y₀) = t. Then Θ(y) = (π(y), t) ∈ target(Φ) (Φ maps its source into its target), so z := π(y) ∈ D, z ∈ B_ρ(c) because y ∈ N, and Λ(z) = Φ⁻¹(π(y), t) = Φ⁻¹(Θ(y)) = y because y ∈ source(Φ). Hence N ∩ F⁻¹(F(y₀)) ⊆ Λ(B_ρ(c)).

14. Steps 6–13 give D, Λ, c, ρ, N with all the asserted properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: dim ker DF(y₀) = n by rank–nullity; extend an isomorphism ker DF(y₀) ≅ ℝⁿ to a linear π with (π, DF(y₀)) injective.
Θ := (π, F) is C¹ with invertible derivative on an open O ∋ y₀; C¹ inverse function theorem restricted to O ∩ W gives a local inverse Φ⁻¹.
D := {z : (z, F(y₀)) ∈ target}, Λ(z) := Φ⁻¹(z, F(y₀)); π∘Λ = id and F∘Λ ≡ F(y₀) on D, so Λ is injective with values in W.
DΛ(z) = DΘ(Λ z)⁻¹ ∘ inl is injective with range ker DF(Λ z).
c := π(y₀) ∈ D, ρ := ε/2 with B_ε(c) ⊆ D, N := source ∩ π⁻¹(B_ρ(c)); points of N on the level set are Λ(π y).

audit.reason: All hypotheses and conclusions match the Lean type. Rank–nullity and extension of the kernel isomorphism produce an invertible straightening derivative. Restricting the inverse-function chart to the open invertibility locus inside W justifies C¹ regularity and the derivative formula at every chart point. That formula proves injectivity and the exact kernel range. The ball and neighbourhood construction proves the required covering inclusion, including n = 0.

subproblem.title: Locality transfer: a.e. on a finite-measure Borel set S, approximate tangent planes of compact C¹ patches χ_k(B̄_k) through x are tangent planes of S
subproblem.statement: Assume (TL): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and all Borel sets A ⊆ B ⊆ U with Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A and every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P: B has approximate tangent space Q at x iff A does (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4). Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let S ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with Hⁿ(S) < ∞. For k ∈ ℕ let D_k ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, χ_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P C¹ on D_k, c_k ∈ ℝⁿ and ρ_k ∈ ℝ with B̄_{ρ_k}(c_k) ⊆ D_k and χ_k injective on B̄_{ρ_k}(c_k). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S the following holds: for every k, every z ∈ B_{ρ_k}(c_k) with χ_k(z) = x and every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P, if χ_k(B̄_{ρ_k}(c_k)) has approximate tangent space Q at x, then S has approximate tangent space Q at x.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (D : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (χ : ℕ → Euclid n → Euclid P) (c : ℕ → Euclid n) (ρ : ℕ → ℝ), MeasurableSet S → μHE[n] S ≠ ∞ → (∀ k, IsOpen (D k)) → (∀ k, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (χ k) (D k)) → (∀ k, closedBall (c k) (ρ k) ⊆ D k) → (∀ k, InjOn (χ k) (closedBall (c k) (ρ k))) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict S), ∀ k, ∀ z ∈ ball (c k) (ρ k), χ k z = x → ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (χ k '' closedBall (c k) (ρ k)) x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 4, bullets 1–2 and 6–7 (Σ_k compact with finite Hⁿ-measure, A_k Borel, two applications of (TL)), and Step 5 (countable union of null sets), stated for an arbitrary sequence of compact C¹ patches. Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n] and Hⁿ⌞A := μHE[n].restrict A; for each k, K_k := B̄_{ρ_k}(c_k), B_k := B_{ρ_k}(c_k), Σ_k := χ_k(K_k), A_k := S ∩ χ_k(B_k).

1. Σ_k is compact and Borel. K_k is a closed ball in the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ, hence compact (isCompact_closedBall). χ_k is continuous on D_k ⊇ K_k (C¹ implies continuous), so Σ_k = χ_k(K_k) is compact (IsCompact.image_of_continuousOn), hence closed and Borel.

2. Hⁿ(Σ_k) < ∞. For each z ∈ K_k ⊆ D_k, χ_k is C¹ at z (D_k is open), so it is Lipschitz on a neighbourhood of z (ContDiffAt.exists_lipschitzOnWith); thus χ_k is locally Lipschitz on K_k, and since K_k is compact it is L-Lipschitz on K_k for some L ≥ 0 (LocallyLipschitzOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith_of_compact). By the Lipschitz image bound (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn), Hⁿ(Σ_k) ≤ Lⁿ·Hⁿ(K_k). On ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), which is finite on the compact set K_k. Hence Hⁿ(Σ_k) < ∞.

3. A_k is Borel. B_k is open, hence Borel; χ_k is continuous on B_k ⊆ K_k and injective on B_k ⊆ K_k; so χ_k(B_k) is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn; ℝⁿ is Polish). As S is Borel, A_k = S ∩ χ_k(B_k) is Borel.

4. Inclusions. A_k ⊆ Σ_k because B_k ⊆ K_k, and A_k ⊆ S.

5. First application of (TL), with (P, n, U, A, B) := (P, n, ℝ^P, A_k, Σ_k). U = ℝ^P is open; A_k and Σ_k are Borel (steps 1, 3); A_k ⊆ Σ_k ⊆ ℝ^P; and for every compact K, Hⁿ(Σ_k ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(Σ_k) < ∞ (monotonicity and step 2). Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A_k and every Q: Σ_k has approximate tangent space Q at x iff A_k does.

6. Second application of (TL), with (U, A, B) := (ℝ^P, A_k, S). S is Borel, A_k ⊆ S ⊆ ℝ^P, and Hⁿ(S ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(S) < ∞ for every compact K. Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A_k and every Q: S has approximate tangent space Q at x iff A_k does.

7. Combining. Intersecting the two full-measure sets, for Hⁿ⌞A_k-a.e. x and every Q: if Σ_k has approximate tangent space Q at x, then so does A_k (step 5), hence so does S (step 6). Since A_k is Borel, this says (ae_restrict_iff') that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P, x ∈ A_k implies [∀ Q, Σ_k tangent Q at x ⇒ S tangent Q at x]; a fortiori this holds for Hⁿ⌞S-a.e. x (Hⁿ⌞S ≤ Hⁿ; ae_restrict_of_ae).

8. Countably many patches. A countable intersection of full-measure sets has full measure (ae_all_iff over k ∈ ℕ), so for Hⁿ⌞S-a.e. x: for every k, if x ∈ A_k then for every Q, Σ_k tangent Q at x implies S tangent Q at x. Also x ∈ S for Hⁿ⌞S-a.e. x (ae_restrict_mem, S Borel).

9. Conclusion. Take such an x, any k, z ∈ B_k with χ_k(z) = x, and Q such that Σ_k = χ_k(B̄_{ρ_k}(c_k)) has approximate tangent space Q at x. Then x ∈ S ∩ χ_k(B_k) = A_k, so by step 8 S has approximate tangent space Q at x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Σ_k = χ_k(B̄_k) is compact and has finite Hⁿ-measure (Lipschitz image of a compact ball).
A_k = S ∩ χ_k(B_k) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin, with A_k ⊆ Σ_k and A_k ⊆ S.
(TL) for (A_k, Σ_k) and for (A_k, S) with U = ℝ^P: a.e. on A_k, Σ_k-tangent Q ⇒ A_k-tangent Q ⇒ S-tangent Q.
Move to Hⁿ⌞S via ae_restrict_iff', intersect over k (ae_all_iff), and apply at x = χ_k(z) ∈ A_k.

audit.reason: The TL antecedent is identical to the parent's. Compactness and local Lipschitz regularity give finite patch measure; restricted injectivity gives Borel open-ball images. Both TL applications satisfy their hypotheses and are used in the correct directions. Restriction identities and a countable intersection yield the conclusion uniformly in Q for every patch through x. No covering assumption or uncountable intersection is needed. The prose proves the exact Lean proposition.

subproblem.title: Slice tangent-plane algebra: range L ∩ g^⊥ = L(ker ℓ), and g = 0 ⇔ ℓ = 0, when ⟨g, L·⟩ = ℓ and g ∈ range L
subproblem.statement: Let m, P ∈ ℕ, let L : ℝ^m → ℝ^P and ℓ : ℝ^m → ℝ be continuous linear maps (ℝ^k = Euclid k), and let g ∈ ℝ^P satisfy g ∈ L(ℝ^m) and ⟨g, L e⟩ = ℓ(e) for every e ∈ ℝ^m. Then (a) g = 0 if and only if ℓ = 0, and (b) L(ℝ^m) ∩ g^⊥ = L(ker ℓ), where g^⊥ = (ℝ∙g)ᗮ = {v ∈ ℝ^P : ⟨g, v⟩ = 0}; in Lean: LinearMap.range L ⊓ (ℝ ∙ g)ᗮ = Submodule.map L (LinearMap.ker ℓ).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m P : ℕ) (L : Euclid m →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (ℓ : Euclid m →L[ℝ] ℝ) (g : Euclid P), g ∈ LinearMap.range (L : Euclid m →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) → (∀ e : Euclid m, inner ℝ g (L e) = ℓ e) → (g = 0 ↔ ℓ = 0) ∧ LinearMap.range (L : Euclid m →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) ⊓ (ℝ ∙ g)ᗮ = Submodule.map (L : Euclid m →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) (LinearMap.ker (ℓ : Euclid m →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 1 (the description of S_t and of T_x), isolated as pure linear algebra for an arbitrary (not necessarily injective) continuous linear map L. Notation: ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product of ℝ^P (inner ℝ), and v ∈ (ℝ∙g)ᗮ iff ⟨g, v⟩ = 0 (Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right).

1. (a), direction g = 0 ⇒ ℓ = 0. Assume g = 0. For every e ∈ ℝ^m, ℓ(e) = ⟨g, L e⟩ = ⟨0, L e⟩ = 0. By extensionality of continuous linear maps, ℓ = 0.

2. (a), direction ℓ = 0 ⇒ g = 0. Assume ℓ = 0. Since g ∈ L(ℝ^m), choose w ∈ ℝ^m with L w = g. Then ⟨g, g⟩ = ⟨g, L w⟩ = ℓ(w) = 0, hence g = 0 (inner_self_eq_zero).

3. (b), inclusion ⊆. Let v ∈ L(ℝ^m) ∩ (ℝ∙g)ᗮ. Choose e ∈ ℝ^m with L e = v. Since v ∈ (ℝ∙g)ᗮ we have ⟨g, v⟩ = 0, so ℓ(e) = ⟨g, L e⟩ = ⟨g, v⟩ = 0. Thus e ∈ ker ℓ and v = L e ∈ L(ker ℓ) = Submodule.map L (ker ℓ).

4. (b), inclusion ⊇. Let v ∈ L(ker ℓ), i.e. v = L e with ℓ(e) = 0. Then v ∈ L(ℝ^m), and ⟨g, v⟩ = ⟨g, L e⟩ = ℓ(e) = 0, so v ∈ (ℝ∙g)ᗮ. Hence v ∈ L(ℝ^m) ∩ (ℝ∙g)ᗮ.

5. By steps 3 and 4 and submodule extensionality (ext v; the membership lemmas Submodule.mem_inf, LinearMap.mem_range, Submodule.mem_map, LinearMap.mem_ker, Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right, ContinuousLinearMap.coe_coe), LinearMap.range L ⊓ (ℝ ∙ g)ᗮ = Submodule.map L (LinearMap.ker ℓ). Together with steps 1–2 this proves (a) and (b). ∎
proof_key_steps: g = 0 ⇒ ℓ(e) = ⟨0, Le⟩ = 0 for all e.
ℓ = 0 and g = Lw ⇒ |g|² = ⟨g, Lw⟩ = ℓ(w) = 0.
v = Le ⊥ g ⟺ ℓ(e) = ⟨g, Le⟩ = 0, giving range L ∩ g^⊥ = L(ker ℓ) by double inclusion.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean proposition agree. The proof correctly uses g ∈ range L to deduce g = 0 from ℓ = 0, proves the reverse implication by extensionality, and establishes the submodule identity by both inclusions. Injectivity is unnecessary. The supplied argument is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Countably many C¹ graph charts cover the regular part of a level set of a C¹ function on an open subset of ℝ^{n+1}
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} open, F : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ of class C¹ and t ∈ ℝ. Then there are, for k ∈ ℕ, open sets D_k ⊆ ℝⁿ, maps Λ_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+1}, points c_k ∈ ℝⁿ and reals ρ_k such that: Λ_k is C¹ on D_k and injective on D_k; for every z ∈ D_k, Λ_k(z) ∈ W, F(Λ_k(z)) = t, DΛ_k(z) is injective and DΛ_k(z)(ℝⁿ) = ker DF(Λ_k(z)); B̄_{ρ_k}(c_k) ⊆ D_k; and every y ∈ W with DF(y) ≠ 0 and F(y) = t equals Λ_k(z) for some k and some z in the open ball B_{ρ_k}(c_k).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (W : Set (Euclid (n + 1))) (F : Euclid (n + 1) → ℝ) (t : ℝ), IsOpen W → ContDiff ℝ 1 F → ∃ (D : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (Λ : ℕ → Euclid n → Euclid (n + 1)) (c : ℕ → Euclid n) (ρ : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ k, IsOpen (D k)) ∧ (∀ k, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (Λ k) (D k)) ∧ (∀ k, InjOn (Λ k) (D k)) ∧ (∀ k, ∀ z ∈ D k, Λ k z ∈ W ∧ F (Λ k z) = t ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ (Λ k) z) ∧ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ (Λ k) z : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid (n + 1)) = LinearMap.ker (fderiv ℝ F (Λ k z) : Euclid (n + 1) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)) ∧ (∀ k, closedBall (c k) (ρ k) ⊆ D k) ∧ ∀ y ∈ W, fderiv ℝ F y ≠ 0 → F y = t → ∃ k, ∃ z ∈ ball (c k) (ρ k), Λ k z = y
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 2, last two sentences (“Γ_t is second countable, so there are countably many such data … with Γ_t = ⋃_k Λ_k(B_{ρ_k}(z_k)). If Γ_t = ∅ …”), made precise with the open neighbourhoods N supplied by the sibling level_set_local_chart (Lean dor_lmbsf_pst_level_set_local_chart). Notation: Γ := {y ∈ W : DF(y) ≠ 0 and F(y) = t}.

1. Case Γ = ∅. Take D_k := ∅, Λ_k := 0, c_k := 0 and ρ_k := −1 for all k. Then D_k is open, every map is C¹ on ∅ and injective on ∅, the properties required for z ∈ D_k are vacuous, B̄_{−1}(0) = ∅ ⊆ D_k (closedBall_eq_empty, as −1 < 0), and the covering property is vacuous because no y ∈ W satisfies DF(y) ≠ 0 and F(y) = t.

2. Case Γ ≠ ∅: local charts. For each y ∈ Γ apply level_set_local_chart to (n, W, F, y₀ := y); its hypotheses hold since W is open, F is C¹, y ∈ W and DF(y) ≠ 0. Choose the resulting data (D_y, Λ_y, c_y, ρ_y, N_y). Since F(y) = t, its conclusions read: D_y is open, Λ_y is C¹ and injective on D_y, and for z ∈ D_y, Λ_y(z) ∈ W, F(Λ_y(z)) = F(y) = t, DΛ_y(z) is injective and DΛ_y(z)(ℝⁿ) = ker DF(Λ_y(z)); B̄_{ρ_y}(c_y) ⊆ D_y; N_y is open with y ∈ N_y; and N_y ∩ F⁻¹(t) ⊆ Λ_y(B_{ρ_y}(c_y)).

3. Countable subfamily. The family (N_y)_{y∈Γ} consists of open sets in the second countable space ℝ^{n+1}, so there is a countable T ⊆ Γ with ⋃_{y∈T} N_y = ⋃_{y∈Γ} N_y (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). T is nonempty: pick y ∈ Γ; then y ∈ N_y ⊆ ⋃_{y'∈T} N_{y'}, so some y' lies in T. Hence T = {e(k) : k ∈ ℕ} for some sequence e : ℕ → Γ (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range).

4. Definition of the sequence. Put D_k := D_{e(k)}, Λ_k := Λ_{e(k)}, c_k := c_{e(k)}, ρ_k := ρ_{e(k)}. Openness of D_k, C¹-ness and injectivity of Λ_k on D_k, the four properties at z ∈ D_k (with F(Λ_k(z)) = F(e(k)) = t) and B̄_{ρ_k}(c_k) ⊆ D_k are the conclusions of step 2 for the point e(k).

5. Covering. Let y ∈ W with DF(y) ≠ 0 and F(y) = t. Then y ∈ Γ and y ∈ N_y ⊆ ⋃_{y'∈Γ} N_{y'} = ⋃_{y'∈T} N_{y'}, so y ∈ N_{e(k)} for some k. As F(y) = t = F(e(k)), y ∈ N_{e(k)} ∩ F⁻¹(F(e(k))) ⊆ Λ_k(B_{ρ_k}(c_k)) by step 2; i.e. y = Λ_k(z) for some z ∈ B_{ρ_k}(c_k). ∎
proof_key_steps: Empty regular level set: use empty charts with ρ_k = −1.
Otherwise apply level_set_local_chart at every regular point y, getting (D_y, Λ_y, c_y, ρ_y, N_y).
Second countability (Lindelöf) gives a countable subfamily of the N_y covering Γ; enumerate it by ℕ.
A regular point y with F(y) = t lies in some N_{e(k)} ∩ F⁻¹(t) ⊆ Λ_k(B_{ρ_k}(c_k)).

audit.reason: The proof uses only its declared local_chart dependency. The open neighbourhoods admit a countable subfamily covering the regular level set; nonemptiness justifies enumeration by ℕ. The empty case is correctly handled by empty domains and negative radii. Every chart property and the stated covering quantifiers follow exactly, without a hidden positivity assumption.
